title: Bprotocol-US11107049-ExchangingEvaluatingVirtualCurrency
universal_lens: The B-protocol establishes a hierarchical, multi-asset reserve-backed token system. The fundamental invariant is the conservation of fractional reserves across a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of token dependencies. Exchange rates are derived deterministically from on-chain state parameters—circulation, total reserve, and fixed reserve ratios—yielding an exact algebraic mapping between arbitrary descendant and ancestor tokens.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, this hierarchical reserve structure maps to a Bayesian belief network over sportsbook liquidity pools. The 'underlying token' represents the base market consensus (e.g., true probability), while 'descendant tokens' represent derivative markets or correlated bets. The reserve ratio acts as a conformal calibration factor, ensuring that marginal updates in sub-markets propagate correctly to the global posterior without arbitrage leakage.
gse_mapping: For GSE situational reasoning, the token DAG models the dependency graph of game states (e.g., possession -> shot attempt -> goal). Exchanging a held token for a requested token mirrors state transitions: if the requested state is an ancestor (e.g., collapsing a specific play into general possession), the exchange burns the descendant and releases underlying resources. If branched, no direct transition exists, requiring a routing protocol.

primitives.name: Reserve Fraction Invariant Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: RESERVE RATIO= 0.2: totalTokensInCirculation = 1000; total Reserve 200 WTH: TOKEN I Sta UNDERLYING TOKEN=ETH; RESERVE RATIO= 0.1.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: R: Total reserve amount (dimensionless token units); \rho: Reserve ratio constant (dimensionless fraction); S: Total tokens in circulation (dimensionless count).
primitives.assumptions: The reserve ratio \rho is a fixed constant defined at token genesis; the underlying asset is perfectly divisible and fungible.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when S \to 0 (division by zero in pricing) or if external shocks cause R < \rho \cdot S (insolvency/under-collateralization).

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the Kelly Criterion's bankroll constraint in GSI, where R is the allocated capital, S is the exposure, and \rho is the optimal betting fraction.

primitives.name: Hierarchical Token Exchange Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: held Token is a descendant of said requested Token Exchanging held Token for its underlying Token said requested Token is a descendant of held said Token Exchanging said held Token for said requested Token and held Token are branched 510 Is requested token?
primitives.latex: \mathcal{E}(T_h, T_r) = \begin{cases} \text{burn}(T_h) \to \Delta U & \text{if } T_h \in \text{Descendants}(T_r) \\ \text{mint}(T_r) \leftarrow \Delta U & \text{if } T_r \in \text{Descendants}(T_h) \\ \emptyset & \text{if branched} \end{cases}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: T_h: Held token type (categorical ID); T_r: Requested token type (categorical ID); U: Underlying reserve asset (dimensionless units).
primitives.assumptions: The token dependency graph is a strict Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG); exchange operations are atomic and deterministic based on graph topology.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the graph contains cycles (infinite minting loops) or if the 'branched' condition lacks a liquidity bridge to route value between disjoint subtrees.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE state-transition logic: collapsing a detailed micro-state (descendant) into a macro-state (ancestor) releases computational/resources, while expanding consumes them.
layer2.telemetry: Transaction success rate conditioned on topological sort distance between T_h and T_r.

primitives.name: State Parameter Retrieval Oracle
primitives.verbatim_quote: Retrieving state parameters of held Token and requested Token from blockchain including Total Tokens in Circulation, Total Reserve, and Reserve Ratio Constant 503.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \Psi: State retrieval function; S_T: Circulation of T; R_T: Reserve backing T; \rho_T: Fixed ratio of T.
primitives.assumptions: The blockchain ledger provides a globally consistent, instantaneous snapshot of all state parameters for any queried token ID.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks under high-frequency concurrent transactions causing temporary ledger inconsistency (race conditions) before block finalization.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's real-time feature extraction layer, pulling current market depth, spread, and volume (S, R, \rho analogs) to compute dynamic edge probabilities.
layer2.telemetry: Latency of state retrieval vs. block time; staleness metric of \Psi(T).

reasoning_traces.think:
The mathematical core of US11107049B2 is the formalization of a hierarchical monetary system on a distributed ledger. We begin with the primitive `reserve_fraction_invariant`, which dictates that for any token $T$, its circulating supply $S$ and reserve $R$ are locked by a constant $\rho$. This creates a rigid algebraic structure where the value of $T$ is intrinsically tied to its underlying asset $U$. The `state_parameter_retrieval` operator acts as the oracle, fetching the tuple $(S, R, \rho)$ to ground all subsequent calculations in empirical on-chain reality. The central duality emerges in the `hierarchical_token_exchange` kernel. By defining tokens as nodes in a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) where edges represent 'backing by', the patent derives a deterministic exchange protocol. If token A is a descendant of B, exchanging A for B is mathematically equivalent to burning A and releasing a proportional amount of the intermediate reserve back up the chain. Conversely, exchanging B for A consumes reserve to mint new A. The failure mode, explicitly noted as the 'branched' condition, occurs when two tokens share no ancestral path; here, the algebraic mapping is undefined, necessitating an external routing mechanism. This structure elegantly prevents hyperinflationary loops because every minting event is strictly bounded by the finite reserve of the root ancestor (e.g., ETH). In the context of GSI/GSE, this provides a robust template for managing nested probabilistic states and resource allocation without circular dependencies.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This patent inherits from the foundational concepts of algorithmic stablecoins and fractional reserve banking, but elevates them via graph theory. Historically, it traces back to the gold standard's fixed ratio ($\rho$) and extends it into a multi-layered, programmable hierarchy. It diverges from traditional fiat by replacing central authority with cryptographic state retrieval (`state_parameter_retrieval`) and automated clearing via smart contracts (`hierarchical_token_exchange`).
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The system models three primary agents: the Issuer (who sets $\rho$ and deposits $R$), the Holder (who possesses $T_h$ and seeks $T_r$), and the Protocol (the immutable rule set). The Issuer acts to maximize seigniorage within the bounds of solvency. The Holder acts rationally to convert assets based on perceived utility or arbitrage opportunities. The Protocol acts as a zero-trust arbiter, enforcing the DAG constraints. Opposing interests arise when Holders attempt to exploit latency in `state_parameter_retrieval` or try to force exchanges in 'branched' regimes, testing the robustness of the veto conditions.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity is enforced by the strict DAG topology; no token can be its own ancestor, preventing recursive minting attacks. Leakage is vetoed by the `reserve_fraction_invariant`: the system physically cannot mint more tokens than the reserve allows given $\rho$. If a transaction attempts to violate $R \ge \rho \cdot S$, the smart contract reverts. Furthermore, the 'branched' condition acts as a hard veto against undefined cross-hierarchy valuations, forcing explicit liquidity provision rather than implicit, potentially flawed, algorithmic bridging.
